translations.answer: Follow the already-recovered workflow for the supported qpOASES_e version, save the actual QP of the failed cycle, rather than only checking the aggregated status of ACADO. The maintainer used `qpOASES_writeIntoFileM` to export a 300×300 Hessian in the acadoWorkspace.H, and after a stand-alone qpOASES_e replay, QP 42/43 was normal, but QP 44 had an non-positive definite Hessian and was abnormal, leading to Cholesky failure; the issue was then passed back to ACADO for side-specific analysis. This result only proves the instance, and does not represent all internal errors caused by a non-positive definite Hessian.
translations.applicability: Directly applicable to the ACADO/qpOASES codegen instance; the method can be transferred, but each failure cycle's root cause must be independently replayed.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and precise references or independent replication have been provided.
translations.details.attempts.0: Enable Levenberg-Marquardt regularization; switch to qpOASES_e 3.1.1; provide ACADO export code and data.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Use `qpOASES_writeIntoFileM(acadoWorkspace.H, 300, 300, ...)` to export per-cycle Hessian and QP data, and then replay in stand-alone qpOASES_e.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The thread does not provide the final fix from the ACADO side; the effective approach is to save the actual QP of the failed cycle, replay in stand-alone, and pass the abnormal Hessian to the upstream generator for localization.
translations.details.environments.0: ACADO code generation; initially used qpOASES 1.3, then switched to qpOASES_e 3.1.1; QP scale is 300×300.
translations.details.limits.0: The root cause only corresponds to the QP 44 provided by the author; other Cholesky failures may still come from different non-positive definite, numerical scale, or data damage.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The maintainer independently replayed QP 42/43/44, confirming the failure follows QP 44 data, and qpOASES recorded as 'wontFix' and suggested contacting ACADO.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How to determine whether the error is due to the solver or the upstream QP construction in ACADO when the qpOASES reports an internal/Cholesky error?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not rely solely on increasing the LM regularization on a real machine in production; first save the failed cycle and offline check the positive definiteness and construction chain.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The maintainer replicated the data: QP 44 Hessian is non-positive definite and visually abnormal, leading to Cholesky failure; the judgment is more likely to be an issue with the ACADO construction.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The old version shows error 31 (Cholesky decomposition failure); after switching to the new version, ACADO returns -1 or -2.

translations.source.title: ACADO embedded qpOASES Cholesky failure requires exporting the specific QP Hessian
translations.title: How to locate whether the Cholesky/internal error in ACADO codegen is due to the solver or upstream QP construction anomaly?
